title.narrative: Program on Circular Economy in Partnership with UNEP in Angul, India

description.narrative:
Angul, an aspirational district in the India state of Odisha, is rich in mineral and natural resources. Given the availability of coal, kyanite, graphite, fireclay, and other raw materials, in recent years it is experiencing further industrial expansion leading to various environmental issues: including loss of biodiversity, transformation of farming lands, pollution, active mines and degradation of water bodies in terms of quantity as well as quality.
In alignment with the global goals and national and subnational plans for sustainable development, the Angul district envisions developing area as the country’s model of mining area development in a challenging environment, with its sustainability embedded in ecological protection, cultural heritage, and human development.
To realise this vision and to build a local level circular, green and inclusive model of economic growth based on judicious use of resources and a life cycle approach, the Angul District Administration in partnership with UNOPS, and the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) aims to develop and implement a first of its kind district level road map on circular and inclusive green economy. The programme will concentrate on the following priority sectors: Plastic; Electronics; Textiles; Aluminium; Steel; Infrastructure; Water management
UNOPS is supporting the District Mineral Foundation Trust (DMFT) Angul by establishing a Programme Management Unit that will advise the district administration in the management, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of the programme. UNEP will work as a knowledge partner in this project who will bring international best practices and learnings in this project.
